rationale: A heading's published name is its display text, and three separate ways of getting that wrong were live at once. (1) The ATX CLOSING RUN: `## Title ##` published `Title ##`, so a document that closed its headings and one that did not produced two different symbols for the same section. (2) A NAME CONTAINING A NEWLINE: a multi-line setext heading's text is its PARAGRAPH, so the previous 'node text minus the last line' fallback returned every line but the underline -- measured, a two-line setext heading published "Multi Line Title\nsecond line of paragraph", carrying an embedded newline into ownerName, the qualified path and every display surface. (3) AN EMPTY HEADING PUBLISHED A MARKER AS A NAME: `#` with no content is `atx_heading > atx_h1_marker` with NO inline child (measured on the pinned wasm), the old fallback returned the marker, and a document of empty headings published a `contains` chain of symbols named `#`, `##`, `###`. That last one is the M60 R7 class -- a name that is not a name -- and it had a second-order effect pinned here: two sibling `##` headings both named `##` collided, so the later headings in this fixture were attributed to the EMPTY `#` as their owner and the whole hierarchy after them was wrong. forbidSymbols is therefore the load-bearing half of this fixture: without it, a regression that republishes markers would still satisfy every expectSymbols entry.

_seamNote.what: The closing-run read is positional (charCodeAt), not a pattern, and the lane's zero-regex property is preserved: the regex census for this analyzer still reports 0 usages.
_seamNote.why: The inline grammar delivers the closing run INSIDE the `inline` child as anonymous `#` tokens, so the text has to be trimmed after the fact. Doing it by character code rather than by regex keeps the lane's strongest measured property -- 0 regex literals, 0 RegExp calls -- while still removing the run.
